messages.content: New trip to frame: Chicago implementation training, Monday through Thursday, probably near River North. I’d fly from Atlanta Sunday evening and come back Thursday if the final lab ends around lunch.

I can help. What are the dates, and do you have a company cap or hotel block yet? The two things I would not assume are the exact venue address and the Thursday end time, because those affect both airport choice and the return flight.

Dates are June 16 to 19, so fly in Sunday June 15. No cap yet. Solo. I want a simple flight, no long layover, and a hotel close enough that mornings are easy. Quiet room for evening work, strong guest ratings, breakfast if it’s available, and dinner nearby. Organizer has not confirmed whether Thursday ends at noon or later afternoon.

Good. For now I would plan around a nonstop into Chicago and keep the return flexible until the lab time is confirmed. If the venue is truly River North, O’Hare is usually the better first search from ATL because it has more nonstop choices and more schedule depth. Midway can work, but I would use it only if the timing or fare is clearly better.
Can you break down O’Hare vs Midway practically? I always mix them up for downtown Chicago.

O’Hare: more airline choices, usually more ATL nonstop options, and a straightforward Blue Line or rideshare into River North. Rideshare can be 35-60 minutes depending on traffic. Midway: smaller and often easier to navigate, with workable downtown access, but fewer carrier choices and it can put you a bit farther from the River North/Merchandise Mart side. For this trip, I’d shortlist O’Hare first and keep Midway as a backup.
What hotel area should I ask for if the training site is somewhere in River North?

Best fit: River North/Merchandise Mart corridor, especially if the venue is west of Michigan Avenue. It keeps mornings short and still has easy dinner options. Second choice: north Loop near the river, usually a little more businesslike and quieter, but possibly a longer walk or short ride. I’d avoid airport hotels for this one; they would make every training morning harder.
I won’t have a car, so restaurant access matters. Breakfast is nice, but I’d rather not sacrifice quiet or location for it.

Then the approval request can be preliminary: fly ATL-Chicago Sunday evening on a nonstop, O’Hare preferred unless Midway has a materially better schedule; return Thursday afternoon only if the lab ends by early afternoon, otherwise hold a later return. Hotel should be flexible/cancellable, guest-rated 4.0 or better where ratings are shown, within an easy walk or short ride of the training site, with a quiet-room request. Note breakfast only if it is listed, and favor places with dinner options on-site or within a short walk.
If they want a list of what still has to be confirmed before I route it, what should I send?

Send this: pending confirmation of the exact venue address, whether a hotel block exists, the final Thursday lab end time, and the travel budget cap. Once those are confirmed, route a Sunday evening nonstop into O’Hare and a Thursday afternoon return if the lab ends near lunch; otherwise use a later return. Hotel target is River North/Merchandise Mart or north Loop near the river, flexible rate, strong guest ratings, quiet-room request, breakfast verified if available, and nearby dinner access.

messages.content: Chicago is confirmed: venue is by Merchandise Mart, and the final lab ends at 1 p.m. on Thursday. I have flight options now but I’m not sure the cheaper connection is worth it.
Great, the 1 p.m. end makes an afternoon return possible. What are the main options and prices?

Option A is Delta nonstop ATL-ORD Sunday 5:45 p.m. to 6:50 p.m., return ORD-ATL Thursday 3:20 p.m. to 6:15 p.m., $428. Option B is a one-stop through Charlotte, $302, gets in Sunday 9:35 p.m. and has a 55-minute connection on the way back. Option C is Midway, $365, workable times but the return is closer to 5 p.m.

I’d submit Option A. It costs more, but it gives you the cleanest travel day, gets you in early enough for dinner and prep, and avoids connection risk. Option B saves $126 but adds a late arrival and a tight return connection. Option C is decent on price, but Midway adds more ground-time friction for the Merchandise Mart area and gets you home later.
Is 3:20 out of O’Hare too tight after a 1 p.m. lab?

It is workable if the 1 p.m. end is real and you do not check a bag. Plan to leave the venue around 1:15-1:30. A rideshare to O’Hare could be 35-60 minutes, so you should still have a reasonable cushion. If the lab tends to run over or there is a required debrief, the later flight is safer but much less convenient.
No checked bag. Seat map on the Delta option is limited, mostly aisle and middle right now.

That is not a reason to switch flights. Book Main Cabin, take the best standard seat available for now, and recheck after ticketing and again at check-in for a window seat. If no window opens, the nonstop schedule is still the better tradeoff.
Can you give me the exact approval line?

Submit: Delta Main Cabin nonstop ATL-ORD Sunday Jun 15, 5:45 p.m.-6:50 p.m.; return ORD-ATL Thursday Jun 19, 3:20 p.m.-6:15 p.m.; estimated $428. Rationale: nonstop both ways, early-enough Sunday arrival for prep, compatible with confirmed 1 p.m. Thursday lab end, and avoids added connection risk. Seat note: select best standard seat at booking and recheck for a window seat after ticketing/check-in.
